s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on Magnetic Resonance Imaging
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The bruise appeared a few days after a twisting injury to the hand
The bruise and pain have persisted for 2 years
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury

shortlist.label: Sclerosing lipogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition and lesional cells positive for CD34

shortlist.label: Fat necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible explanation for the persistent painful bruise and soft tissue swelling with mixed inflammatory infiltrate

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous pseudotumor
shortlist.why_kept: Could account for the heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on MRI and the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesional cells are spindled and ovoid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli, and immunohistochemistry is positive for CD34

raw.rationale: The presence of a painful bruise that persisted for 2 years, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli, along with immunohistochemistry strongly positive for CD34, are consistent with Nora's lesion, a rare condition characterized by a subcutaneous nodular lesion with a history of trauma.

rejected.label: Fat Necrosis
rejected.why: While fat necrosis can occur after trauma, the pathology and immunohistochemistry results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans
rejected.why: This condition typically presents as a slowly growing plaque or nodule, often without a history of trauma, and the immunohistochemistry results do not match.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis is a systemic disease that typically presents with multiple lesions and systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Atypical Lipomatous Tumor
rejected.why: The pathology and immunohistochemistry results do not support this diagnosis, as atypical lipomatous tumors typically have a different morphological and immunophenotypic profile.
